results.name: why_question
results.playtest: C s3 t6, C s1 t4

turns.prompt: Why is Texas at the top of the capacity chart? Is it really the state with the most capacity?

checks.description: the reply names the answer to SELECT t_state FROM turbines GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY SUM(t_cap) DESC LIMIT 1

turns.output:
Texas is at the top because the chart’s underlying SQL sums turbine capacity (`t_cap`) by state, then sorts the results in descending order—but it only keeps the top 10. **In the full comparison, Texas is second, not first:** California has 235.8 MW across 103 turbine records, while Texas has 192.85 MW across 103 records.

I added a state capacity comparison table. One caveat: the query sums turbine-level capacity, so this comparison uses that measure consistently across states.
